sources.repository: Internet Archive / Media History Digital Library
sources.researchNote: The advertisement uses the pre-release title Der glückliche Herr Fünf, after Alice Berend’s novel Herr Fünf. It credits Heinz Hilpert as director, Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann with the music, Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender in the leading role, and Pax Film GmbH as producer. The released film is documented elsewhere as Ich will Dich Liebe lehren.

media.title: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender as Figaro — Ross Verlag postcard, c. 1928
media.altText: Photographic postcard portrait of the baritone Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender in costume as Figaro.
media.publicCaption: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender as Figaro in Rossini’s Il barbiere di Siviglia, on a signed Ross Verlag artist postcard of about 1928. He took the lead in Ich will Dich Liebe lehren, singing Tränen in der Geige and Schön ist das ganze Leben.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unknown; signed artist postcard, Ross Verlag, c. 1928; private collection, via Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The Wikimedia Commons file records the postcard as published more than seventy years ago without a public claim of authorship, which places an anonymous work out of copyright in the European Union, and as published before 1 January 1931, which places it out of copyright in the United States. The photographer is not named on the card.

contributions.scopeNote: Recorded the song with the Marek Weber Orchestra; the recording is published on the Jube Pops compilation of Walter Jurmann’s film songs. He also played the lead in Der glückliche Herr Fünf, the film the song comes from, as the trade advertisement announces.
